thread:
maria: Heads-up: we're seeing ~30% regression in NCCL allreduce bandwidth in euc1 after last night's kernel (6.1.12) + OFED 6.0 roll.
tj: Which cluster/instance types? any single-node repro?
maria: Affected machines are p4d-like pools in euc1 (gpu-pool-3). Happens across multiple racks. NVLINK looks fine; NV peer stats normal. CPU jumps during allreduce and ib counters show repeated dma mapping errors.
raj: Can you paste the dmesg / kernel logs from one of the nodes?
maria: Here are the relevant lines from one of the nodes (truncated):

```
[ 2378.451234] efa: registered device efa0
[ 2378.453678] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.1: enabling SR-IOV
[ 2380.112345] efa0: dma_map_page failed -22
[ 2380.112360] efa0: falling back to CPU-copy path for TX
[ 2380.112366] efa0: failed dma_map_sg: rc=-22
[ 2380.112370] rdma: efa0: build tx bounce buffer, using cpu copy
```

maria: Also saw userspace NCCL logs showing fallback from ibv_post_send path to staged copy.
infra-bot: Detected abnormal RDMA DMA mapping failures on node gpu-103 (alert id: rdma-dma-2101). Generating incident ticket INC-1122.
tj: If dmesg explicitly says dma_map_page failed, that points to IOMMU/SG mapping issue or dma mask change from kernel driver. Any iommu remapping changes in the kernel module? Was VFIO toggled?
yun: We did flip iommu=pt -> iommu=1 on a small subset last cycle for PCIe device isolation. Could be related.
raj: Can you run a quick ib_send_bw and compare to pre-roll numbers? Also check /proc/interrupts and vfio status.
maria: ib_send_bw from two nodes in the same rack:

```
# before (pre-roll)
# ib_send_bw -d mlx5_0
MAD: 95.3 GB/s
# after (post-roll)
MAD: 62.1 GB/s
```

maria: nvidia-smi topo shows expected NVLINK, no degraded GPU interconnect. nvidia driver unchanged. CPU user% during allreduce jumps from ~35% to ~70% on host.
tj: Sounds like EFA/OFED is falling back to non-RDMA copy path (pinned host staging). That would explain CPU up and bandwidth down.
raj: Could also be that the new OFED changed dma mapping constraints (dma_mask/IOMMU) leading to too-large addresses being rejected and driver opting for bounce buffers.
yun: Quick check: cat /sys/module/efa/parameters/enable_dma_mapping (exists?) and check iommu groups/ dmesg for vfio messages.
maria: There's an efa param enable_dma_mapping=1. vfio messages show "IOMMU: page table damaged" warnings around the same time as dma_map errors.
raj: Repro script idea: run a small NCCL allreduce with NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=0 and strace the process to see ibv_post_send path errors, and capture kernel logs.

```
# repro cmd (quick)
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0 ./nccl_allreduce_test
```

maria: Rolling back kernel+OFED on a single canary rack improved throughput back to ~92% of baseline.
tj: Good. That suggests the rollout introduced incompatible DMA behavior. Plan: canary rollback for the rest of euc1 tomorrow 03:00 UTC, pause the global rollout. We need a proper RCA before reapplying.
raj: I'll build a small automated repro that toggles iommu boot args and runs ib_send_bw + nccl_allreduce so we can validate a fix. Assigning self -> INC-1122.
yun: I'll update the runbook with the rollback steps and note the IOMMU checks. Also notify kernel/driver vendors with dmesg snippet.
infra-bot: Incident INC-1122 created: "EFA DMA mapping failures after kernel+OFED rollout -> NCCL bandwidth regression". Priority: high. Pager duty: on-call infra.

maria: Short-term mitigation: pin affected pools to previous kernel bundle, disable next-stage rollout, and enable extra monitoring for dma_map failures.
tj: Long-term: we should add an automated pre-roll smoke that runs ib_send_bw and a small nccl workload and verifies no dma_map_errors in dmesg.
raj: Agreed. I'll add that to the rollout playbook and the CI gating test.
yun: FYI: vendor support request opened with logs attached. We'll escalate if we don't have a vendor patch within 48h.
maria: Thanks team. I'll start the canary rollback ticket and coordinate with capacity so we don't impact production jobs. :thumbsup:

tj: Ack. Keep updates in this thread.
raj: Repro script ETA 4h, posting link here when ready.

maria: (later) repro script: https://internal.corp/repro/INC-1122 (attached) — shows dma_map fail reproduced under iommu=1 kernel boot arg.

tj: Great, saved. Next steps: execute canary rollback 03:00 UTC, monitor, then decide on full rollback vs vendor patch.

maria: Closing loop: canary rollback completed, metrics trending back to baseline. Continuing with vendor engagement and runbook changes.
